summary.headline: Stove Kraft Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 41.3% YoY to INR480.6 crore, with EBITDA up 50.9% to INR53.8 crore and margin at 11.2%.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the strongest first quarter since inception, with revenue of INR480.6 crore (up 41.3%), gross profit of INR190.4 crore (up 46%) and PAT of INR17.1 crore (up 63.5%). Induction Cooktops grew 315.9% YoY and were about 27% of revenue, while small appliances and gas cooktops moderated because capacity and people were diverted to induction. Price hikes in domestic and export markets were used to pass on input cost inflation, supporting gross margin expansion of 127 bps. Working capital rose to 45 days on festive inventory build-up, and management guided to Q2 growth despite a high base.

financial_highlights.change: Higher than Q4 FY26; better than Q1 FY26 (69 days)

segments.name: Induction Cooktops (ICT)
segments.commentary: Grew 315.9% YoY and contributed 27% of revenue (about INR130 crore per analyst calculation). Management expects ICT to reach at least 20% of revenue for the year and about 2x last year on an annualised basis.

segments.name: Pressure Cookers
segments.commentary: Grew 41.3% YoY; management says it is the largest by volume at current run rate, with capacity additions under way.

segments.name: Non-stick cookware
segments.commentary: Grew 21.8% YoY and contributed 21% of revenue.

segments.name: Small appliances and gas cooktops
segments.commentary: Moderated temporarily due to capacity diversion to induction; small appliances still make up 27.5% of revenue mix. Management says capacity has since been augmented.

segments.name: Channels
segments.commentary: E-commerce 31.8% of revenue, general trade 28.6% (up 56.2% YoY, strongest in three years), exports 15.3%, modern retail 13%, and retail 8.7% (up 86.3% YoY). Added 17 franchise stores in the quarter, targeting 500 Pigeon exclusive outlets by end-2027.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 revenue expected to grow YoY over Q2 FY26 (about INR475-480 crore base), though not necessarily at Q1's growth rate.
Gross margin expected to improve at least 1% YoY; management views 40-42% as the sustainable gross margin band.
EBITDA margin targeted to rise at least 1 pp YoY, reaching 14-15% within two to three years.
Long-term PAT margin trajectory of 7-8% over two to three years, per management comments on a TV interview.
Non-induction categories targeted to grow about 15%+ consistently, with a stated aim near 20%; overall growth targeted at 15-20%.
Exports plus IKEA expected to reach about 15% of revenue in the current and next year; IKEA full-scale could be 5-6% of business. IKEA supplies to start in Q2 FY27.
Retail: profitable above INR2.5 lakh sales per store per month; currently about INR4.3 lakh, target at least INR5 lakh.
Triply cookware circle production in China JV expected by December 2026; automated pressure cooker line ready by end Q3.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing facilities set up in the last few quarters are all up and running, per management.
Pressure cooker capacity being added to meet unmet demand; a fully automated pressure cooker line is being set up, ready by end of Q3 FY27.
Small appliance capacity was diverted to induction and infrared products in Q1; management says it has since been augmented.
Triply cookware: JV with a Chinese partner, reportedly among the largest facilities in China; machines being installed; commercial production expected by December 2026.
Chimney range converted from AC to BLDC motors (all but one model); built-in hobs also being pushed.
Outsourced some manufacturing via job work in Q1 to meet demand; management expects this to normalise as in-house capacity comes up.
demand_pricing: Induction cooktop demand remains above pre-war levels; management expects traction to continue but not at the initial spike levels.
Cost-plus pricing model: domestic price increases taken and export buying prices revised upward to pass on input cost inflation.
Gross margin improvement attributed to price corrections and a favourable mix, including stainless steel pressure cookers outgrowing aluminium.
Q1 exchange-offer programme (mainly in EBOs and general trade) cited as a regular seasonal driver; GPOs up about 80% and general trade up about 50%.
Festive calendar spread across Q2 and Q3 (Onam in August, Dussehra in early October, Diwali in November).
South region about 50% of general trade contribution; North and West growing faster from a smaller base.
Working capital: inventory build-up for festive season; management plans straight-line production through the year to smooth working capital.

Other expenses rose to about 18% of sales, driven by job work (+1.2 pp), marketing (+1.2 pp; spend about 3.5-3.6% of sales), franchise commission (about 1% of sales; franchise mix 55-56% vs 43%), and CSR front-loading (about INR94 lakh, about 3% of PBT).

qa_highlights.question: How should growth look for Q2 and Q3 FY27, given festive timing and LPG-related demand anxiety?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 and Q3 are the larger quarters and festive demand is well spread (Onam in August, Dussehra in early October, Diwali in November). It expects strong performance vs last year, with induction traction continuing but below the initial spike levels.

qa_highlights.question: Will margin improvement be sustainable, and are further price hikes still needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domestic prices were raised and export buying prices revised upward to pass on input cost inflation. It expects at least 1% YoY gross margin improvement and sees current margin levels as sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: How is the export business trending, and what is the outlook for exports plus IKEA?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports were about 12% of revenue last year and management expects exports plus IKEA to reach about 15% of revenue in the current and next year. IKEA is treated as deemed export and was not in Q1; IKEA supplies start in Q2 FY27, and a full-scale IKEA business could be 5-6% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Can Q2 grow over last year's high base of about INR475-480 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 will be strong and growth is expected, though not necessarily at Q1's rate. Growth is across pressure cookers (up 41%), small appliances (capacity augmented) and cooktops, and across channels.

qa_highlights.question: When will PAT margins exceed 5%, and what is the path to 7-8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said financial leverage is already setting in and incremental growth will flow to PAT. It sees gross margin settling at 40-42% on an ongoing basis, with the trajectory towards 7% PAT margin, but gave no year-specific timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Where will working capital days settle by end of FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 45 days in Q1 FY27 versus 69 days in Q1 FY26 and 75 days in Q4 FY25, and said it is moving to straight-line production to smooth working capital through the year. It did not give a year-end target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise to about 18% of sales, and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Job work rose 1.2 pp of sales, marketing rose 1.2 pp (spend about 3.5-3.6% of sales), franchise commission was about 1% of sales (franchise mix 55-56% vs 43%), and CSR was front-loaded at about INR94 lakh (about 3% of PBT). Management said job work and CSR are not continuing costs and should normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the finance cost increase despite low debt?
qa_highlights.answer: YTD finance cost is INR7 crore, or 1.6% of sales versus 2.1% a year ago. Working capital interest fell about INR2 crore, offset by ROU lease and an asset lease taken in Q3 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the induction cooktop run rate versus pre-war levels, and how much of FY27 revenue can it be?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give monthly run-rate figures. It said demand is above pre-war levels and it expects ICT to be at least 20% of revenue for the year and about 2x last year on an annualised basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the retail economics and store target?
qa_highlights.answer: Stores are profitable above INR2.5 lakh sales per store per month; current run rate is about INR4.3 lakh, with a target of at least INR5 lakh. 17 franchise stores were added in Q1, targeting 500 Pigeon exclusive outlets by end-2027.

risks_watch: Sustainability of growth after the GST-cut and induction-driven spike; management concedes induction will not repeat initial spike levels, and non-induction growth targeted at 15%+ with a stated aim near 20%.
Q2 and Q3 growth against a high base (Q2 FY26 about INR475-480 crore); management guided growth but gave no number.
Input cost and rupee pressure: pricing is cost-plus, with exports repriced upward; any lag in price pass-through could compress the gross margin band of 40-42%.
Elevated other expenses (about 18% of sales) from job work, marketing, franchise commission and CSR; management says these normalise but gave no timeline.
Working capital at 45 days, above Q4 FY26, due to festive inventory build; straight-line production plan not yet proven.
Execution of new capacity: automated pressure cooker line ready by end Q3 FY27, Triply circle production in the China JV by December 2026, and IKEA supplies starting Q2 FY27.
Dependence on exchange-offer programmes in Q1 (GPOs up about 80%, general trade up about 50%); the revenue contribution was not quantified.
key_quotes: We are pleased to report on our strongest ever first quarter performance since inception.

While the category witnessed extraordinary growth last year, demand continues to remain substantially above pre -war level, indicating a structural shift in consumer adoption rather than a temporary spike.
It will not be at the level of the spike that was there in the beginning of the quarter, but then we still see very high growth in the Induction Cooktop followed by cooking category.
Q1 is one of the smallest quarter of the year.
These are not, continuing costs, but definitely there was elevated during the first quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, premiumisation and the export and IKEA pipeline. Cautious on the induction spike, where management conceded demand will not stay at initial levels, and evasive on quantities such as IKEA absolute revenue, exchange-programme contribution and the monthly induction run rate.
